text: Hi, welcome to the Mumbai edition of Is My Architecture. I am Mani, a solution architect
with AWS. I am joined by Manju Soma, CTO of Arvind Internet. Hi Manju, welcome to the show.
Thanks Mani. Arvind Limited is an iconic brand in India and across the world. I myself am a big
power user of Arvind Brands. Can you tell us a little bit about Arvind Internet?
Arvind Internet is a B2B SaaS company building a suite of products called Omni. Omni addresses
retail commerce by powering commerce on multiple channels and creating retail journeys for our
brands and their customers. Omni is built for scale, is cloud first and also built for high availability.
What kind of footprint is Omni trying to address? Omni has rolled out to 35 plus brands across the globe.
Some of them are internal urban group brands and some of them are external brands. You are looking
at about 6000 offline stores, multiple different warehouses on Omni and we have enabled commerce
on marketplaces. For example, we have enabled marketplaces like Flipkart and Amazon on Omni.
So Omni channel is multi-channel journey for customers on Omni product.
That's a lot of stores and marketplaces that this platform is trying to address. Can you walk us
through the architecture of Omni platform? Yeah, I mean we have all the entire external traffic
from our brands on customers to our WAF, right? WAF helps us in mitigating the unwanted malicious traffic,
including bot and DDoS attacks. Once, I mean the filter of traffic is done, the traffic moves from WAF to our
different microservices. We are fully on microservices architecture. We have 70 plus microservices supporting our business.
So, the traffic goes through the 70 plus microservices on Kubernetes. We are fully on Kubernetes containers.
Security is a big factor in the world in load balancing the traffic and load balancing the traffic.
And from the application load balancers, the traffic moves from the load balancers to our different microservices.
We are fully on microservices architecture. We have 70 plus microservices supporting our business.
The traffic goes through the 70 plus microservices on Kubernetes where fully on Kubernetes containers.
Security is a big factor in e-commerce platforms. I also see that you are using API Gateway.
Could you explain to us, you know, what kind of use cases that API Gateway is being used for?
Yeah. The API Gateway serves us two different purposes. All the API are, some of them are external,
or some of them are internal, right? The load balancing and the external traffic for,
goes through the API gateways for our microservices and goes from the API Gateway to our microservices.
Between the microservices, we have 70 plus microservices. The throttling of traffic happens through the API Gateway.
I see that you are using multiple types of data store and RDS, MySQL database as well as an elastic cache.
Can you explain what kind of use cases do each of these data store use?
Yeah. So, we have a lot of inventory. We get a lot of inventory data from our brands, right?
And we also do enable commerce for our brands, right? So, and along with that, we have a lot of non-transactional data,
for example, click-throughs and stuff like that, right? So, from the microservices, we have data flowing into our cache.
From cache, it goes into different data sources, right? So, the transactional data gets stored in MySQL.
The non-transactional data gets stored in Cassandra. We also use, we are power users of elastic cache.
Elastic cache primarily helps us in processing and enriching data, right?
So, what kind of database sizes are we talking about in the RDS?
Oh, we are looking at large inventory for brands and commerce as well as non-transactional data.
It runs into several terabytes.
I see that you are also using a message queue here. Can you explain to us how message queue plays a role here?
Omni is an asynchronous product, right? The traffic moves asynchronously across microservices and across different data stores, right?
So, from the microservices world, there's a push and there's a pull, right?
And all of this is handled by different message queues.
Also, we use queues predominantly to manage our traffic for our different data stores as well as cache.
Handling DevOps for 70 plus microservices should be a big challenge. How do you do DevOps in Arvindit?
Omni is a huge footprint. We have a large code repository. The entire code repository is managed on Bitbucket and Fabricator.
The code is packaged and processed using Jenkins. From the Jenkins, the images are pushed to elastic container registry to be pushed into production deployment on the containers.
Scaling in retail is a big challenge. How do you handle scaling in the Kubernetes platform?
Scaling in Omni channel comes in various flavors. Primarily scaling happens for peak season. Peak season for Omni channel or for our business,
for Omni channel or for our brands is for end of season and festivals, right?
You are looking at 5X kind of a scaling model, right?
We enable scaling by vertical and horizontal scaling. For containers, we primarily use horizontal power scaling and DC-2 scaling.
And you are looking at roughly about 3 to 5 million active sessions at any given point of time during the peak season.
That's a lot of user shopping for products on your platform. Now, what's next in terms of the roadmap for the Omni channel platform?
We talked about how retail is getting disrupted. Multiple channels are getting added. Retail is changing.
So, we are rethinking retail. We are continuing to evolve Omni to address this and enable commerce for Omni.
Along with that, we have tons of data. Customers and brands are expecting a lot of data insights. For that, we are building data lake.
So, for the containers and for the Omni product to work, we are investing and building out on the self-serve model.
Thanks for sharing your architecture. Thanks for joining. This is my architecture.
